feature: The next arrow you draw keeps the last one's look, fades included
summary: Style one arrow, box, line, Pen path, title or picture on a video, fade included, and the next one of that kind arrives looking exactly the same. Fade In and Out does both ends in one click (⌃⌥F), and every fade row now reaches all the picked things at once, in one undo.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open the tutorial recording. Walks: Scripts/playtest/the-next-arrow-fades-like-the-last-walk.json and Scripts/playtest/the-whole-look-carries-over-walk.json (compare with Scripts/playtest/look-carries-over.py).

evaluate: Is Fade In and Out where you reached for it, right under Start and End on the arrow's right-click?
Six arrows faded with one click: is that the experience you wanted, or would you rather the first arrow also arrived faded by default?
Is a second at each end the right length for the first Fade In and Out, before anything is remembered?
Should a picture pasted into a screenshot (not a video) also keep the last picture's look? Today only pictures on a video do.
rough: Clicks for the try path (two stills, three arrows each, all fading in and out), counted from the walk: before, each arrow took a right-click, More, Fade In, 1s, then a right-click, More, Fade Out, 1s, so 8 clicks x 6 arrows = 48. After: 2 (right-click and Fade In and Out on the first arrow), or 1 key (⌃⌥F); the other five arrive faded.

The table, read off the saved document by look-carries-over.py on the build before this change and on this one (draw a first, style it, draw a second, compare). Arrow: opacity, shadow, thickness, arrow style, head, head size carried before; fade in, fade out, ends did not; all carry now. Line: opacity, shadow, thickness carried; fades and ends did not; all carry now. Box: opacity, shadow, corner radius carried; fades did not; all carry now. Oval and highlight: opacity and shadow carried; fades did not; all carry now. Pen path: thickness carried; opacity, shadow, fades, ends, dashes did not; all carry now. Words (a title on a video): opacity, the added shadow and fades did not carry; all carry now (font, size, weight and colour already did). Picture on a video: opacity, shadow and fades did not; all carry now. 26 settings failed before, 0 now.

Settings that deliberately do not carry: the words of a title or a caption, where a thing sits, its size, and its start and end on the timeline (an arrow on a freeze still takes exactly the hold); text alignment, which was already a choice made per block; a pasted copy, which keeps the look of what it was copied from.

Not walked: measurements (the measure tool caught no edges on open video, so the walk could not land one). Their fade is remembered by the same code and pinned by RememberedLooksTests; their colours were already remembered in measurement styles. Colour and Pen corner shapes were not set in the walk: colour has been remembered per shape since before this task, and corners go with ends and dashes in one record.

Pictures pasted into a still screenshot keep arriving as themselves. Chose remembering a picture's look only on a video over everywhere because redlining a screenshot pastes many unrelated pictures and should never be second-guessed.

Chose ⌃⌥F for Fade In and Out over Premiere's ⇧D (Apply Default Transitions to Selection) because a shifted letter would fire while typing a capital D, and ⌃⌥F sits beside the existing ⌃⌥I and ⌃⌥O; neither Photoshop nor Premiere gives ⌃⌥F anything (UX-PATTERNS §7).

Add Transition moved from a placed picture's or title's top level to its More menu to make room for Fade In and Out within the ten-row limit; it only appears where two placed things meet (UX-PATTERNS §7 does not cover menus; logged as my call).
No mock covers this surface: it is a right-click row and remembered defaults, not a new panel.
